questions.q: What are the three Ps of trauma described in the summary?
a: Personalization, pervasiveness and permanence
Panic, paralysis and passivity
Pain, protest and progress
Pressure, pessimism and pride
questions.why: Lesson 1 introduces Martin Seligman's three-P model: personalization, pervasiveness and permanence.

questions.q: What does personalization mean in this context?
a: Blaming yourself for something you could not control
Believing the sadness will never end
Letting grief spread into every area of life
Hiding your feelings from friends
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes personalization as blaming yourself for an event you could not control.

a: Keeping hope alive while taking practical next steps
Waiting for a rescue that may never come
Believing everything will return to normal
Avoiding the company of others while grieving
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines grounded hope as keeping hope alive while taking practical steps forward.

questions.q: What does the Andean rugby team example illustrate?
a: Resilience can come from a group, not only from within
Survival depends mainly on physical strength
Hope fades quickly in extreme conditions
Strangers rarely cooperate under stress
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the Andes crash survivors to show resilience within and between people.

questions.q: What kind of help should you offer a grieving friend?
a: Specific offers, like getting groceries
A general offer to help if needed
Space and silence until they reach out
Advice on how to move on quickly
questions.why: Lesson 3 says specific offers such as groceries signal genuine help better than a vague offer.
